text:
My heart sets out from my body to yours

on its last journey.

Offshoot of light,

water of the ages that is born lost in you.

Come to my thirst. Now.

After everything. Before.

Come to my long thirst held at bay

by mouths, scant springs.

I want that deep harp that in your belly

lulls wild children,

I want that taut wetness throbbing in you,

that wetness of water that burns in you.

Woman, soft muscle.

The skin of a kiss between your breasts

with their darkened swell

sails in my mouth

and measures blood.

You too. And it's not too late.

We can still die in each other:

that place belonging to no one is yours and mine.

Woman, tenderness of hatred, ancient mother,

I want to enter, penetrate you,

poison, flame, absence,

bitter and bitter sea, pass through you.

Each cell is female, open earth,

open water, something opening.

I was born to enter you.

I am the arrow in the back of the dying gazelle.

I exist to know you,

a grain of anguish in a bird's heart.

I will be over you, and all women

will have a man over them everywhere.

translation.title: My Heart Sets Out
